q: 1. Soil can exist in .............
explain: Depending on conditions, soil can be a three-phase system (solid-water-air), two-phase (dry solid-air, or saturated solid-water), or approach single-phase, so all apply.

q: 2. Soil is considered as .............
explain: Soil is generally treated as a three-phase system consisting of solid particles, water, and air.

q: 3. The degree of saturation in soils can be defined as the ratio of
options: water by weight to the dry soil weight
vol. of water to the gross vol. of soil
vol. of water to vol. of voids in soils
wt. of the water to wt. of soil
explain: Degree of saturation Sr = Volume of water / Volume of voids, expressed as a percentage; it tells how much of the void space is filled with water.

q: 4. The most accurate method of determining the water content in a sample of soil is
explain: Oven drying at 105-110°C to constant weight removes only free/pore water precisely, making it the standard, most accurate laboratory method (IS: 2720 Part 2).

q: 5. Generally soils is considered as
explain: Soil is a three-phase system consisting of solid particles, water, and air voids.

q: 6. Fully saturated soil is considered as
explain: In a fully saturated soil, all voids are filled with water, leaving only two phases: solids and water.

q: 7. The specific gravity of a soil is the ratio of the unit weight of the soil solids to that of water at a temperature of .............
explain: Specific gravity of soil solids is conventionally referenced to water at 27°C in Indian standard practice.

q: 8. The principle involved in the relation γsub = γsat − γw is .............
explain: This relation for submerged unit weight is derived from Archimedes' principle of buoyancy.

q: 9. Degree of saturation of a soil is generally
explain: The degree of saturation (S) represents the ratio of water volume to void volume, ranging from 0% (dry) to 100% (saturated).

q: 10. The most commonly used specific gravity of a soil in soil mechanics is .............
explain: Grain (true) specific gravity of the solid particles is the value most commonly used and reported in soil mechanics.

q: 11. The water content of soil is defined as the ratio of
options: volume of water to volume of given soil
volume of water to weight of air in voids
Weight of water to weight of air in voids
weight of water to weight of solids of given mass of soil
explain: Water content w = Weight of water / Weight of solids (dry weight), expressed as a percentage — the standard geotechnical definition.

q: 12. The relationship between void ratio (e) and porosity ratio (n) is:
explain: Since n = e/(1+e), rearranging gives e = n(1+e), the correct relation linking porosity and void ratio.

q: 13. A fundamental equation of void ratio (e), specific gravity (G), water content (ω) and degree of saturation (Sr) is
explain: From Se = wG (since Sr·e = w·G), rearranging gives e = wG/Sr, the fundamental phase-relationship equation.

q: 14. The degree of saturation for fully saturated soil is .............
explain: A fully saturated soil has all void spaces filled with water, giving a degree of saturation of 1 (100%).

q: 15. You are given a sample of soil containing coarse grains to determine its water content, you will use
explain: For coarse-grained soils, the pycnometer method (using known specific gravity) is the standard quick technique to back-calculate water content.

q: 16. The void ratio for saturated soil is equal to the ......... of water content and specific gravity of solid
explain: For saturated soil, e = wG, i.e. void ratio equals the product of water content and specific gravity.

q: 17. The minimum water content at which the soil retains its liquid state and also possesses a small shearing strength against flowing, is known
explain: The liquid limit is the water content at the boundary between liquid and plastic states, where the soil just begins to show small shear resistance.

q: 18. The ratio of the volume of air voids to the volume of voids, is called .............
explain: Air content is defined as the ratio of the volume of air voids to the total volume of voids.

q: 19. The void ratio of soil is
options: the ratio of voids to solids in volume
the ratio of voids to gross volume
the ratio of solids to voids in volume
the ratio of solid volume to gross volume
explain: Void ratio (e) is defined as the volume of voids divided by the volume of solids.

q: 20. The degree of saturation for the moist soil is about .............
explain: Moist (partially saturated) soil typically falls in the 50-75% degree of saturation range.

q: 21. The ratio of volume of air void to the volume of voids, is known
explain: Air content (ac) is the ratio of the volume of air to the total volume of voids.

q: 22. The approximate void ratio in sandy soils is .............
explain: Sandy soils typically have void ratios around 0.6 in their natural, moderately dense state.

q: 23. The ratio of volume of voids to the total volume of the given soil mass is known as
explain: Porosity (n) is defined as the ratio of the volume of voids to the total (bulk) volume of the soil.

q: 24. The change of moisture content of soils, changes the
options: value of the angle of repose
explain: Moisture content influences frictional/angle-of-repose behaviour, compaction effort needed, and cohesive strength — hence all listed properties are affected.

q: 25. Theoretically, the void ratio in soils can have the following values
explain: While void ratios can technically exceed 1 in organic soils or soft clays, for typical theoretical soil models, it is often discussed in terms of being less than 1 or within specific ranges. Note: The answer key specifies 'b'.

q: 26. The ratio of weight of water to the weight of solids in a given mass of soil, is known as
explain: Water content (w) is the ratio of the weight of water to the dry weight of solids, usually expressed as a percentage.

q: 27. The specific gravity of sandy soils is .............
explain: Sandy (quartz-dominated) soils typically have a specific gravity around 2.65-2.70.

q: 28. If a soil undergoes a change in shape and volume by application of external loads over it, but recovers its shape and volume immediately after removal of the load, the property of the soil to be
explain: Immediate and complete recovery of shape/volume after unloading is the defining characteristic of elastic behaviour.

q: 29. The degree of saturation in soils can be defined as the ratio of
options: water by weight to the dry soil weight
volume of water to the gross volume of soil
volume of water to volume of voids in soil
explain: Degree of saturation (S) specifically measures how much of the void space is occupied by water.

q: 30. The water content of soils can be accurately determined by .............
explain: Oven drying at 105-110°C is the standard reference method for accurate water content determination.

q: 31. The relationship between void ratio (e) and porosity ratio (n) is
explain: The standard relationship between these two parameters is e = n / (1-n) or n = e / (1+e).

q: 32. The specific gravity of soil solids is determined by .............
explain: The pycnometer (or density bottle) method is the standard laboratory technique for determining specific gravity of soil solids.

q: 33. Void ratio, e of a soil can
explain: Void ratio must always be greater than zero because a soil mass must contain some voids.

q: 34. The functional equation for specific gravity (G) water content (w), void ratio (e) and degree of saturation (Sr) is
explain: The fundamental soil mechanic relation is Se = wG. Rearranging for e gives e = wG/S.

q: 35. The fundamental relation between percentage Air voids na, specific gravity (G), water content (w) and dry density (gamma_d) is
explain: The formula relates dry density to air voids and specific gravity; the options in the image are slightly different, but 'a' is the intended answer key choice.

q: 36. The ratio of the difference between the void ratio of the soil in its loosest and fully dense state is termed as
explain: These terms—relative density and density index—are used interchangeably to describe how dense a soil is relative to its limits.

q: 37. The specific gravity of sandy soils is
explain: The specific gravity of most inorganic soils like sand typically falls around 2.65.

q: 38. Relationship between void ratio e and porosity n is given by .............
explain: The standard relation is e = n/(1-n), equivalently expressed as e = n(1+e).

q: 39. The relation between dry density (gamma_d), bulk density (gamma) and water content (w) is
explain: Dry density is calculated by dividing bulk density by (1 + water content).

q: 40. For testing a saturated clay for shear strength, the test recommended, is
explain: For saturated clays, the quick, simple unconfined compression test is commonly recommended since no confining pressure is needed to get the undrained shear strength.

q: 41. A pycnometer is used to determine
explain: A pycnometer is a standard laboratory vessel used to find the specific gravity and water content of soil.

q: 42. The percentage of the porosity of loose sand is in the range of
explain: Loose sands have higher void spaces, typically resulting in porosity between 40% and 50%.

q: 43. The percentage of the porosity of clay is in the range of
explain: The answer key indicates 'b' (20-30%) for the specific range of clay porosity in this context.

q: 44. The soil sample contains volume of void 0.2 and volume of soil is 0.30 then find the void ratio & porosity of soil
explain: Void ratio e = Vv/Vs = 0.2/0.3 = 0.67. Porosity n = Vv/Vt = 0.2/(0.2+0.3) = 0.40.

q: 45. A soil sample contains a degree of saturation is 30%, find the percentage of air voids
explain: If the voids are 30% filled with water, the remaining 70% must be filled with air.

q: 46. A soil sample have following characteristics- S=50%, G=2.6, W=30%, find the void ratio, e
47. Which method is quickest to find the water content of soils
explain: The calcium carbide method provides rapid results (minutes) compared to the standard 24-hour oven-drying method.

q: 48. The water content of soils can be accurately determined by
explain: Oven drying is the standard laboratory method for the most accurate determination of water content.

q: 49. The water content in a soil sample when it continues to loose weight without loosing the volume, is called
explain: Shrinkage limit is the water content below which further loss of moisture does not cause any further reduction in volume — i.e., weight reduces but volume stays constant.

q: 50. The shearing strength of the following soil will be excellent when compacted and saturated .............
explain: Well-graded sand (SW) compacts to high density with good interlocking, retaining good shear strength even when saturated.
